summary: Shuming Liang was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Shuntian Middle School (~1906–1911) and held a post in the philosophy department at Peking University from 1917.

Shumpei Ueyama worked in philosophy and Japanology. After studying at Taihoku High School and Kyoto University, he served at Kyoto University from 1954 (professor in 1968; emeritus 1982–1984) and was president of Kyoto City University of Arts (~1986–1989).
Shun Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He was an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and a part-time lecturer at Otani University, attested in 2014.

Shun'ei Hirai specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1950–1954) and the University of Tokyo (~1956–1974), and served at Komazawa University from 1964 as lecturer, professor, and vice president, becoming emeritus professor in 2001.
Shunei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College, attested in 1995.
Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Bukkyo University, attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shunji Hosaka works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1976–1985) and held positions at Reitaku University (~1991–2005) and Chuo University (~2005).

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1930–1933). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1953–1980), where he became emeritus professor.

Shunryu Suzuki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Gyokujun So-on, Dojun Kato, and Ian Kishizawa, and at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served as head priest at Zoun-in, Rinsouin, and Sokoji.

Shunsho Manabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1968) and held positions at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, serving as professor from ~1999 to 2010.
Shunsho Terakawa worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1955) and held a post at Otani University (~1966–2000), where he became an emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011 and served as a part-time lecturer there, attested in 2012.

Shuntaro Matsuyama worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and held posts at Bigakko, Tama Art University, Kokugakuin University, and as professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1972–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993 and served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1952), earned a doctorate from Toyo University by 1962, and served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1965–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He held a post at Komazawa University (~1949–1987), where he became emeritus professor.
Shwe Zan Aung worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1932–1936). He served as a professor at Rissho University from ~1960 to 1983.

Shōren Ihara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi and held posts at Taisho University, including Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014).
